title.value: Investigating the Barriers to Physician Adoption of an Artificial Intelligence-Based Decision Support System in Emergency Care: An Interpretative Qualitative Study
title.justification: The title is explicitly stated in the beginning of the document and reflects the core focus of the study, which is on understanding the barriers to physician adoption of an AI-based decision support system in emergency care.
title.quote: Investigating the Barriers to Physician Adoption of an Artificial Intelligence- Based Decision Support System in Emergency Care: An Interpretative Qualitative Study

analysis.description: This research examines the implementation of an AI-based decision support system in emergency care at a large Academic Health Center in Canada. The study focuses on the barriers to adoption by analyzing perceptions of healthcare managers, AI developers, physicians, and nurses. It emphasizes the importance of technical, human, and organizational factors, highlighting the need for strategies to adapt AI systems to healthcare contexts.

type.justification: The study involves an in-depth case study at an Academic Health Center, triangulating data collection through interviews, observations, and document analysis, which are typical empirical methods.
type.quote: An in-depth case study was performed at the ED, triangulating data collection methods and sources in an ethnographic approach to make sense of actors' perceptions of the DSS implementation process.

name.justification: The paper focuses on the implementation and adoption of AI-based decision support systems in healthcare, specifically in emergency care settings.
name.quote: The development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems to support diagnostic decision-making is rapidly expanding in health care.

name.justification: The research specifically investigates a decision support system that leverages AI for aiding emergency care.
name.quote: This research examines the implementation of an AI-based decision support system (DSS) in the emergency department of a large Academic Health Center (AHC) in Canada.

name.justification: The AI-based decision support system analyzed in the study is implemented within the context of emergency care.
name.quote: This research examines the implementation of an AI-based decision support system (DSS) in the emergency department of a large Academic Health Center (AHC) in Canada, focusing specifically on the question of end-user adoption.

name.value: Deep Learning Algorithm for Diagnostic Decision-Making
name.justification: The study discusses the use of a deep-learning algorithm in a decision support system for medical diagnostics in emergency care.
name.quote: The DSS is a diagnostic technology based on a deep-learning algorithm using clinical data and evidence-based results from the scientific literature.

is_contributed.justification: The paper discusses the application of the existing deep-learning algorithm in their DSS, rather than introducing a new model.
is_contributed.quote: The DSS is a diagnostic technology based on a deep-learning algorithm using clinical data and evidence-based results from the scientific literature.

is_executed.justification: The deep learning model is part of the DSS that was implemented and tested at an Academic Health Center, thus it was executed as a part of the pilot project.
is_executed.quote: In November 2018, an AI-based DSS was tested for implementation as a pilot project in the AHC's ED.

is_compared.justification: The paper focuses on the barriers to adoption of the DSS rather than comparing its performance with other models.
is_compared.quote: Our analysis of the implementation process revealed several barriers identified by research participants that limited the DSS integration into clinical processes and workflow.

referenced_paper_title.justification: The paper references other works on AI in medicine which supports the credibility and context of the deep learning model discussed.
referenced_paper_title.quote: P. Hamet, and J. Tremblay. Artificial intelligence in medicine. Metabolism. 69 (2017), S36-S40.
